mainEntity.name: What does Loading, Transloading and Container Services include?

acceptedAnswer.text: Container loading and unloading, and transloading between truck, container and warehouse — counted, sorted and restacked for the inland leg, with cross-docking and warehouse staging.

Transloading is the process of moving a shipment from one mode of transport to another — from an ocean container to a truck, in the most common case. The contents of one load unit are unloaded (destuffed) and loaded into another load unit that suits the next leg better. It tends to happen near port terminals or inland satellite terminals — anywhere the freight's vehicle stops being the right vehicle.

mainEntity.name: How is transloading different from cross-docking and deconsolidation?

acceptedAnswer.text: Cross-docking means freight never enters storage: it leaves on outbound LTL or FTL the same shift. Deconsolidation means breaking one consolidated container apart by destination, purchase order, or SKU into many outbound loads. A transload often includes one or both, plus storage between legs where needed.

mainEntity.name: What do free time, demurrage, and detention mean for my shipment?

acceptedAnswer.text: Free time is the window before charges start; the last free day (LFD) ends it. Past LFD, the terminal charges demurrage for a box sitting at the terminal, and the carrier charges detention (per-diem) for a box kept outside the terminal. Moving the box inside free time — and transloading promptly — is how those charges are avoided.

mainEntity.name: What if my container is overweight?

acceptedAnswer.text: Where a container genuinely cannot be permitted to destination, transloading its cargo into domestic trailers removes the container weight from the equation; for some lanes that is cheaper than permitting even when a permit is available. Scope and pricing are quoted per job.

Per job, at one flat rate. We review the full scope — the container, the freight, the sort, any rework, staging and the onward legs — and agree the price in writing before dispatch. There is no per-container rate and no automatic or instant estimate; the estimate is human-made. Guaranteed Flat Rate or Your Move is Free!

mainEntity.name: Do you offer bonded warehousing, customs brokerage or FTZ services?

acceptedAnswer.text: No — and the distinction matters. The Virginia Inland Port is a U.S. Customs-designated port of entry and sits within Foreign Trade Zone #185, which is operated by the Virginia Port Authority. Those are the port's statuses, not ours. We are a private handling operation near the port: we do not broker customs, we operate no bonded warehouse and no foreign-trade zone activity, and we claim no refrigerated or cold-chain handling and no hazmat handling. What we do is the physical work — unload, count, split, stage, rework and deliver the freight.

mainEntity.name: What if the load includes a very heavy item?

acceptedAnswer.text: If a transload involves a high-mass asset in the 1,500–3,500 lb range, that asset moves under Structural Integrity Relocation (SIR), with floor deflection analysis to L/360, as part of the same flat-rate job. SIR is not claimed for transloading generally; it applies only where such an asset is actually involved.
